answer: Each identity claims one shale slope plot beside a wander trail and posts a 75-credit bond on erosion pins. Each epoch the keeper reports pin exposure below a dated ember layer, plus the walker count; auditors recompute expected exposure from the count times a public shale wear table, and a reused pin serial, copied count, or exposure beyond 5% burns the bond. A first plot costs 34 credits, each later plot adds 6, so plot 1000 costs 6028 and 1000 plots cost 3,031,000 in fees with 75,000 bonded. A rented-pin ring fails: one pin set cannot survey two slopes at once. One honest plot costs 34.
